easter-1.quote: And so, dearly-beloved, if we unhesitatingly believe with the heart what we profess with the mouth, in Christ we are crucified, we are dead, we are buried; on the very third day, too, we are raised.
easter-1.who: St. Leo the Great, Sermon on the Lord’s Resurrection
easter-1.question: Which grudge or habit, buried with Christ, will you leave in the tomb today instead of carrying it with you into the Easter season?

easter-2.quote: But the hour had now come when the joy, in some measure announced by the angels, who forbade her tears, was to succeed the weeping.
easter-2.question: What sorrow are you still weeping over? Listen for Christ calling your name today, and place that one grief in his hands.

easter-3.quote: For they saw that He was dead, and they had no hope that He would rise again; all their hope was gone.
easter-3.question: Where has your hope gone quiet, as though it were over? Tell Jesus plainly today what you had hoped for, as the two on the road did.

easter-4.quote: Yes, for a word from the divine Scriptures, made to sound in the ear, doth more than fire soften the hardened soul, and renders it fit for all good things.
easter-4.who: St. John Chrysostom, Homilies on Matthew
easter-4.question: When did Scripture last warm your heart? Give ten minutes today to one Gospel passage, reading slowly until a single word stays with you.

easter-5.quote: And He departed from our eyes, that we might return into our heart, and there find Him.
easter-5.question: Christ vanishes from sight so that we may find him within. Where will you stop today, in silence, to look for him in your own heart?

easter-6.quote: For nails had pierced His hands, a spear had laid open His side: and there the marks of the wounds are preserved for healing the hearts of the doubting.
easter-6.question: Which of your own wounds could Christ’s wounds heal? Bring it honestly to him today, and pray Thomas’s words: “My Lord and my God.”

easter-7.quote: Forego vengeance, forgive offences: exchange severity for gentleness, indignation for meekness, discord for peace.
easter-7.who: St. Leo the Great, Sermon on Lent
easter-7.question: Whose peace have you been withholding? Choose one offence to forgive or one discord to soften today, and give Christ’s greeting a concrete word or act.

easter-8.quote: Believers know the body of Christ, if they neglect not to be the body of Christ.
easter-8.question: After receiving Christ in the Eucharist, how will you become what you received? Name one way you will be bread for someone this week.

easter-9.quote: An hundred and fifty fishes were taken—by Simon’s net from the water;—but there were taken by his preaching,—out of the bosom of Baptism,—ten thousands and thousands of men,—a draught of the sons of the Kingdom.
easter-9.who: St. Ephrem the Syrian, Hymns for the Epiphany
easter-9.question: Where have you worked all night and caught nothing? Hand that task to Christ today, and try one thing at his word.

easter-10.quote: He also forthwith forgave Peter, for he wept most bitterly. And if you weep bitterly Christ will look upon you and your guilt shall leave you.
easter-10.question: Where have you failed Christ as Peter did? Bring that failure to him in honest tears today, expecting forgiveness rather than reproach.

easter-11.quote: If, then, the care of feeding is the proof of loving, whosoever abounds in virtues, and yet refuses to feed the flock of God, is convicted of not loving the chief Shepherd.
easter-11.who: St. Gregory the Great, Pastoral Rule
easter-11.question: Christ asks you what he asked Peter: do you love me? Answer him this week by feeding someone with your time, patience, or practical help.

easter-12.quote: He hath brought me forth in the narrow ways, wherein few walk, of His righteousness; not for my merit’s sake, but for His Name’s sake.
easter-12.who: St. Augustine, Expositions on the Psalms
easter-12.question: Which narrow way is the Shepherd leading you through now? Name it, and follow him one step today rather than choosing the easier path.

easter-13.quote: And whither go we, but to Him, and by what way go we, but by Him?
easter-13.question: Where are you trying to reach God by some other road? Take one decision today and ask what going by Christ himself would look like.

easter-14.quote: Seest thou that the love of God is intertwined with our own, and connected like a sort of chain?
easter-14.who: St. John Chrysostom, Homilies on John
easter-14.question: Whose love has been a link in the chain that holds you to God? Return it today by loving one person in a concrete way.

easter-15.quote: For when the branch is cut off, another may spring up from the living root; but that which is cut off cannot live apart from the root.
easter-15.question: What has cut you off from the root: neglected prayer, resentment, busyness? Choose one thing to reconnect you with Christ this week, and begin today.

easter-16.quote: And He is called the Comforter, because He comforts and encourages us, and helpeth our infirmities
easter-16.who: St. Cyril of Jerusalem, Catechetical Lectures
easter-16.question: In which weakness do you most need the Comforter? Pray “Come, Holy Spirit” today, and ask for his help in that one place.

easter-17.quote: He that will have joy of himself shall be sad; but he that will have his joy of God will ever rejoice, because God is everlasting.
easter-17.question: Where are you seeking a joy that cannot last? Place your joy in God today by thanking him for three gifts no one can take away.

easter-18.quote: We bless the Lord our God, who gathered us together to spiritual joy. Let us be ever in humility of heart, and let our joy be with Him.
easter-18.question: With whom could you share this Easter joy? Make a call or share a meal with one person today, and give thanks together.

easter-19.quote: So ought we also to rejoice, who have been thought worthy to know the Son of God; to rejoice, not in thought alone, but to show it also by our actions.
easter-19.who: St. John Chrysostom, Homilies on John
easter-19.question: How could you show your joy in Christ by action today, not only by feeling? Choose one deed of obedience or kindness, and do it gladly.

easter-20.quote: Let joy be wholly of hope to come, desire be wholly of eternal life. Let all sighings breathe after Christ.
easter-20.question: What do you long for that only eternal life can satisfy? Pray today for that full joy, and set aside one small thing that dims it.

easter-21.quote: For indeed the preacher drinks out of his own cistern, when, returning to his own heart, he first listens himself to what he has to say.
easter-21.who: St. Gregory the Great, Pastoral Rule
easter-21.question: Before you speak of Christ to anyone, which word do you most need to hear yourself? Listen to it in prayer, then share it with one person.

easter-22.quote: He who speaks to you in person has what He has not left, and yet He came; for by coming He departed not thence, nor has He forsaken us by returning thither.
easter-22.question: Where do you most need to remember that Christ has not left you? Say “You are with me” before one hard task today.

easter-23.quote: For then He sent the Holy Ghost: by whom the disciples being fulfilled preached with confidence the Word of God, that Churches might be collected.
easter-23.who: St. Augustine, Expositions on the Psalms
easter-23.question: The Spirit gives courage to witness. Where could you speak or act as a disciple this week with a boldness you usually lack?

easter-24.quote: And so, dearly-beloved, let us rejoice with spiritual joy, and let us with gladness pay God worthy thanks and raise our hearts’ eyes unimpeded to those heights where Christ is.
easter-24.who: St. Leo the Great, Sermon on the Lord’s Ascension
easter-24.question: As Christ is lifted up, which earthly worry will you set down? Spend a quiet minute today looking toward him with thanks.

easter-25.quote: Let us not then be taken up with the appearances of temporal matters, neither let our contemplations be diverted from heavenly to earthly things.
easter-25.who: St. Leo the Great, Sermon on the Lord’s Resurrection
easter-25.question: Which temporal concern keeps pulling your thoughts downward? Choose a moment today to turn toward heaven on purpose, and let one anxiety rest.
